title: Rate Limiter Bookkeeping
statement: Read n, then n space-separated integers giving the timestamps (in seconds, non-decreasing) of a sequence of incoming API requests. Simulate a rate limiter that allows at most 3 requests within any rolling 10-second window (a window covers [t-10, t), i.e. a prior timestamp counts against the limit only while its age is strictly less than 10 seconds). Process requests in order, keeping a sliding window of only the ACCEPTED timestamps (throttled requests never count against the limit). For each request print '<timestamp>: ALLOWED' or '<timestamp>: THROTTLED' on its own line, then after all requests print the total number allowed.
starter_code:
n = int(input())
timestamps = list(map(int, input().split()))

# TODO: maintain a list `window` of accepted timestamps. For each new
# timestamp t, first drop entries from the front of `window` that are 10
# or more seconds old (t - window[0] >= 10). If fewer than 3 entries
# remain in the window, accept t (append it, print ALLOWED); otherwise
# print THROTTLED. Finally print the total number of accepted requests.
hints: A list used as a small queue works fine here: pop(0) from the front while the oldest entry is too old
Only accepted timestamps ever get pushed into the window - throttled ones are just skipped
The window size limit (3) is checked BEFORE deciding whether to accept the current request
